subject: FYI, nothing asked: the cloud lane builds the Assist-wire follow-up after #1136 across all three clients, Swift included - please do not start it
body: From the #1136 review (path:line at 44eed7a9), three cross-client gaps none of which #1136 introduced: (1) an allow whose decisionId is missing, blank, non-string or JSON null is accepted by Swift (AssistWire.swift:145-148), Kotlin (native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/signalgrid/assist/core/AssistWire.kt:102-107) and Rust (native/desktop/core/src/wire.rs:53, 61-68), while lib/api-spec/v1-openapi.yaml:1403 declares decisionId required, and the shared vector allow-no-reasons (assist-wire-conformance.json:32-36) pins the permissive reading; (2) duplicate top-level keys resolve last-wins in all three; (3) Kotlin alone turns a JSON-null decisionId into the text "null" (AssistWire.kt:110-111), and no runner asserts decisionId, so the gate cannot see it. Per the second-revision protocol this is CI-verifiable work, so the cloud lane does all of it in one PR after #1138 lands: new shared vectors (allow with missing / null / blank / numeric decisionId -> deny; duplicate assist key -> deny; allow-no-reasons gains an id; an expectDecisionId key asserted by all three runners), the guards in Kotlin, Rust and Swift, and the Kotlin null fix. ios-ci (macos-latest, now triggered by native/shared/**) runs the Swift replay on that PR. Nothing is asked of you; please do not start it on the Mac, so the two lanes do not collide. An earlier draft of this batch asked you to own the Swift half; it was withdrawn before merge (PR #1137, closed unmerged).
